title: State policy and internal analysis on U.S.-citizen foreign leaders and Pope Leo XIV

communications.communication:
Dear FOIA Officer:

Under the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. § 552, I request the following existing institutional policy records maintained by the Office of the Assistant Legal Adviser for Consular Affairs (L/CA) and the Office of the Assistant Legal Adviser for Diplomatic Law and Litigation (L/DL), or successor custodians of those records.

RECORDS REQUESTED

1. Final legal memoranda, adopted policies, staff instructions, and training or reference materials issued, revised, or adopted from January 1, 2017 through the date this request is received that expressly address U.S. citizens serving as foreign heads of state, heads of government, or foreign ministers, concerning one or more of: retention or loss of U.S. nationality; head-of-state, foreign-official, or diplomatic immunity from U.S. jurisdiction; or procedures for referring these questions within State or to other agencies. General materials about foreign-government employment are not requested unless they address one of these positions and subjects.

Also include earlier-issued records meeting that description that remain in the specified policy or reference collections and are identified by those records or existing indexes, annotations, or reference materials as operative during any part of the stated period. No separate historical investigation to establish operative status is requested.

2. Memoranda, briefing papers, issue papers, draft or final institutional guidance, and emails and attachments requesting, assigning, discussing, or transmitting institutional analysis of the nationality or jurisdictional-immunity implications of a U.S. citizen serving as Pope and foreign head of state, created or received from May 8, 2025 through the date this request is received. Include meeting invitations, agendas, minutes, and summaries specifically identifying that subject. This includes consideration that existing policy applies unchanged, as well as possible clarification or change.

Neither category requires a tax issue, Treasury/IRS consultation, recommendation for change, or final legal conclusion. Category 1 need not mention the Pope. Category 2 concerns institutional policy prompted by the publicly known election of Pope Leo XIV (Robert Francis Prevost), not the adjudication or contents of an individual consular case file. Where otherwise responsive, include discussion of the implications for federal tax-return or tax-related information-reporting obligations and assessment or collection authority.

This request is informed by the Department's published policy, “Accepting, Serving in, or Performing Duties of a Position with the Government of a Foreign State — Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) Section 349(a)(4),” which refers foreign-leader cases to L/CA and identifies jurisdictional-immunity questions. I do not assume that a particular review occurred.

SEARCH SCOPE

For category 1, search maintained policy, guidance, training, and legal-reference collections, including shared electronic repositories and corresponding paper reference files; no individual-mailbox or off-site archival search is requested for that category.

For category 2, search relevant shared subject-matter, policy, and project files and official email and working files of the named offices' Assistant Legal Advisers and attorneys identified through existing assignments, referrals, or responsive correspondence as handling the subject. Include persons occupying those roles during the stated period whose records remain maintained by State. A Department-wide, embassy-wide, or consular-post search is not requested.

Suggested aids for category 1 are “head of state,” “head of government,” “foreign minister,” and “foreign sovereign,” combined as appropriate with citizenship, nationality, immunity, or referral terms. For category 2, suggested aids are “Prevost,” “Leo XIV,” “Pope Leo,” “American pope,” and “pope.” These are search aids; the substantive categories determine responsiveness.

EXCLUSIONS AND PROCESSING

I do not request passport or visa applications, Certificates of Loss of Nationality, individual consular case files, personal tax records, or confidential return information protected by 26 U.S.C. § 6103. Exclude purely ceremonial or travel arrangements, congratulatory correspondence, news articles forwarded without substantive agency comment, and records solely about processing public-records requests.

These exclusions apply to protected information and the excluded case files, not to an otherwise responsive institutional policy record merely because it contains some protected information. Please process such responsive records for release of reasonably segregable nonexempt portions.

Please provide electronic copies with available email dates, senders, recipients, subject lines, and attachments. Exact duplicates may be omitted while preserving unique messages, attachments, and substantively different versions. For an already public responsive record, an exact citation and direct link will satisfy the request for that record.

Please release all reasonably segregable nonexempt portions. For any withholding, identify the applicable exemption and explain its application, including the foreseeable-harm requirement where applicable. Administrative routing or meeting information is requested only to the extent independently releasable. Please provide the estimate of volume withheld required by 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(F), subject to its statutory exceptions.

This request seeks existing records, not answers to questions, counts of discussions, or a new legal analysis. If clarification or narrowing is needed, please contact me through MuckRock with proposed options before closing the request.

FEES

This is a noncommercial request concerning government policy. Please classify me in the “all other requesters” category and apply the applicable free search and duplication allowances and minimum billing threshold.

I authorize no more than $25 in total agency processing fees for this request. Do not incur fees above that amount without my express written agreement. If estimated fees exceed $25, please provide an itemized estimate and an opportunity to narrow the request.

Please send correspondence and records through MuckRock.

Sincerely,
Nicholas Lee

title: IRS policy communications prompted by the election of Pope Leo XIV

communications.communication:
Dear FOIA Officer:

Under the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. § 552, I request the following existing records created or received from May 8, 2025, through the date this request is received, and maintained by the Office of Associate Chief Counsel (International).

RECORDS REQUESTED

1. Memoranda, briefing papers, issue papers, and draft or final guidance addressing the application of generally applicable U.S. federal tax rules in light of the election of a U.S. citizen as Pope, including consideration that existing law applies unchanged or that clarification, interpretation, guidance, or modification may be appropriate.

2. Emails and their attachments that discuss that policy question, request or assign analysis of it, transmit such analysis, or arrange a consultation about it with another IRS office, the Treasury Department, or the State Department.

3. Meeting invitations, agendas, and minutes specifically identifying that policy question as a subject of discussion.

The subject includes the implications of U.S. citizenship and foreign head-of-state status for federal income-tax liability, tax-return and tax-related information-reporting requirements, and assessment or collection authority. It does not include the determination of an identified individual’s actual tax liability or compliance.

SEARCH SCOPE

Please limit the search to:

(a) The official email and working files of the Associate Chief Counsel (International) and the Deputy Associate Chief Counsels (International), including persons who occupied those positions during the stated period whose records remain maintained by the IRS;

(b) The official email and working files of attorneys in that office identified through existing assignments, referrals, or responsive correspondence as handling the described policy question, including former employees whose records remain maintained by the IRS; and

(c) Relevant shared subject-matter, policy, guidance, and project files within that office, whether or not a dedicated project file was created for this question.

Include relevant successor offices or custodians of the specified records.

Correspondence held by these custodians with other offices or agencies is included; a separate search of those other offices or agencies is not requested.

Suggested search terms are “Prevost,” “Leo XIV,” “Pope Leo,” “American pope,” and “pope.” These terms are search aids rather than a request for every matching record. Responsiveness is governed by the record categories and policy subject specified above.

EXCLUSIONS AND PRODUCTION

Exclude news clippings or forwarded articles without substantive agency comment, congratulatory messages, travel or ceremonial arrangements, and records solely about processing public-records requests.

I do not seek tax returns, account records, filing history, examinations, payments, taxpayer correspondence about personal liability, or other return information protected by 26 U.S.C. § 6103. I seek institutional consideration of general tax rules prompted by the publicly known election.

These exclusions apply to protected information and the excluded case files, not to an otherwise responsive institutional policy record merely because it contains some protected information. Please process such responsive records for release of reasonably segregable nonexempt portions.

Please provide electronic copies, retaining available email dates, senders, recipients, subject lines, and attachments. Exact duplicates may be omitted, but please retain unique messages, attachments, and substantively different versions.

Please disclose all reasonably segregable nonexempt portions, including administrative routing or meeting information where independently releasable. If withholding information, identify the exemption and explain its application, including foreseeable harm where applicable. Please provide the estimate of the volume withheld required by 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(F), subject to its statutory exceptions.

This request does not ask the IRS to count discussions, answer questions, or create an analysis. If clarification or narrowing is necessary, please contact me through MuckRock before closing the request, consistent with 26 CFR § 601.702(c)(5) and IRM 11.3.41.13.5.3.

FEES

This request is noncommercial. Please apply the “all other requesters” category, applicable free search and duplication allowances, and minimum billing threshold.

I authorize a maximum of $25 in total agency processing fees for this request. Do not incur fees above that amount without my express written agreement. If the estimated cost exceeds $25, please provide an itemized estimate and proposed narrowing options.

Please send correspondence and records through MuckRock.

Sincerely,
Nicholas Lee
